title: Sharing a Flat: Good or Bad?

passage.title: Sharing a Flat: Good or Bad?

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Many young people share a flat with others, especially in big cities where rents are high. In London, a typical one-bedroom flat can cost more than a thousand pounds a month, but a room in a shared flat costs about half of that. Sharing is not only about money, however. It also changes the way people live, for better and for worse.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The main advantage is the cost. As well as rent, flatmates split the bills for electricity, gas and the internet. This can leave more money for travelling, studying or saving. Another advantage is company. People who live alone sometimes feel lonely, whereas flatmates can eat together, watch films or just talk about their day. For students who move to a new city, this can make it much easier to make friends.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, sharing a flat can cause problems. The most common are noise, mess and arguments about money. In a survey of two thousand young people, almost half said that they had argued with a flatmate about cleaning, and a third said they had been annoyed by a flatmate who did not pay a bill on time. Privacy is another issue, especially when the bathroom or the kitchen is shared by four or five people.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: How can these problems be avoided? Experts give several suggestions. First, choose your flatmates carefully. It is better to live with someone who has similar habits, for example someone who also goes to bed early, than with your best friend. Second, agree on rules from the beginning, such as a cleaning timetable. Writing the rules down helps, because it is harder to argue about something that everyone has signed.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Finally, it is wise to read the contract carefully. In many countries, all the tenants are responsible for the full rent, which means that if one person leaves, the others must pay their share. If you plan to share, it is a good idea to ask the landlord what happens in that situation before you sign.
